title: Cluster 01 DRILL: Viral Structure and the Phage Cycles
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 4 · 8 questions · 76 marks · 31 parts · one mark per minute, so a little over an hour and a quarter · every question is an actual exam paper question
los_html:
Learning outcomes, against the questions that test them.
1(e) structural components of viruses, including enveloped viruses and bacteriophagesQ1(a), Q1(b), Q1(c), Q1(d), Q2(a), Q2(c), Q2(d), Q4(d), Q5(a), Q7(a), Q7(b), Q8(d)
1(e) interpret drawings and photographs of virusesQ1(a), Q2(a), Q2(c), Q4(d), Q5(a), Q7(a)
1(e) the viral enzymes a virion has to carry, and whyQ3(a), Q3(c), Q5(b), Q7(b), Q8(c)
1(f) how viruses challenge the cell theoryQ4(a), Q4(b), Q4(d)
1(f) concepts of what is considered living, obligate intracellular parasitismQ4(b), Q4(c), Q4(d)
2(d) viral genome: DNA or RNA, single or double stranded, linear or circular, segmented or notQ1(c), Q1(d), Q2(a), Q2(b), Q2(c), Q7(b)
2(d) positive against negative sense, and what each forces the virion to carryQ3(a), Q3(b), Q3(d)
2(e)i the lytic cycle, all five stagesQ5(b), Q7(b), Q7(c), Q8(c), Q8(d)
2(e)i the lysogenic cycle, prophage, induction, and lambda phageQ6(a), Q6(b), Q6(c), Q6(d)
2(e)i virulent against temperate phageQ6(a), Q6(d), Q8(a), Q8(b)
2(e)i host range and receptor specificityQ7(b), Q7(c), Q8(d), Q8(e), Q8(f)
reach-back Book 1: amino acids, peptide bonds, levels of protein structureQ5(a)
reach-back Book 2: nucleotides, phosphodiester bonds, the double helixQ5(a)
reach-back Book 2: genome organisation, histones, linearity, chromosome numberQ2(a), Q2(c)
reach-back Book 2: the central dogma, transcription, translation, DNA replicationQ3(b), Q3(c), Q3(d), Q5(b)

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required ANSWERS and not just for duplicated labels. Q1 reading an unfamiliar enveloped virus and saying where each part came from · Q2 three viruses that are on no syllabus, described on the axes the outcome names · Q3 what the genome type forces the virion to carry · Q4 the cell theory tested statement by statement · Q5 the lytic cycle end to end, plus protein against nucleic acid as molecules · Q6 why a phage would ever choose not to kill its host · Q7 phage anatomy mapped to function, and what happens when the receptor does not fit · Q8 the lytic cycle turned into a therapy, and where the therapy fails. The one shared idea in the set is that viruses are acellular, which Q4(b) needs alongside the crystallisation and ATP arguments and Q4(c) needs alongside the host-resources argument; the two parts are marked on different points and neither answer is the other. Every other pair was checked at the level of the paragraph the scheme demands, and no two questions need the same one.

Nothing from Books 5 to 9, and nothing from Clusters 2 or 3 of this Book. The influenza and HIV reproductive cycles, antigenic shift and drift, and the whole of bacterial genetics are later clusters, so no question here needs them. Where influenza appears it is only as a genome to compare against, at the level of eight negative-sense segments. Vaccines, antibodies and immunity are Extension Topic A and are out of scope in every answer.
